params.question: In the syndromic approach to sexually transmitted diseases, treatment is withheld until the causative organism is confirmed by laboratory testing.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: That is incorrect. The syndromic approach does the opposite — it treats empirically at the first visit based on the presenting syndrome, without waiting for laboratory confirmation. This is necessary because in most Indian primary care settings, organism identification is unavailable or impractical, and delaying treatment means the patient leaves untreated and continues transmitting.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The syndromic approach treats all probable pathogens of a recognised syndrome at the first visit itself, precisely because laboratory diagnosis is often unavailable, delayed, or the patient cannot return for results. This is the official NACO strategy under the National AIDS Control Programme.

params.question: After determining that a genital ulcer is painful, which pair of clinical features best helps distinguish between chancroid and herpes genitalis?

answers.text: Ulcer edge character and the pattern of lymph node involvement

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Chancroid produces a soft ulcer with undermined edges and often a unilateral, tender, suppurative bubo. Herpes genitalis presents as grouped vesicles rupturing into shallow ulcers with bilateral tender nodes and systemic symptoms. These features reliably separate the two at the bedside.

answers.text: Duration of incubation period and the patient's occupation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incubation periods of chancroid (3–10 days) and herpes (2–12 days) overlap considerably and are rarely known precisely. Occupation is not a morphological discriminator. Ulcer morphology and lymph node pattern are far more reliable.

answers.text: Response to benzathine penicillin and serological titre

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Benzathine penicillin is the treatment for syphilis, not for chancroid or herpes. Neither serological titres nor penicillin response help distinguish between two painful ulcer conditions.

answers.text: Presence of a groove sign and oral mucosal patches

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The groove sign (the inguinal ligament bisecting swollen nodes) is characteristic of lymphogranuloma venereum, and oral mucous patches suggest secondary syphilis. Neither belongs in the painful ulcer differential.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the bedside features: chancroid has soft, undermined edges with a suppurative bubo, while herpes shows grouped vesicles with bilateral nodes and systemic symptoms.
Well done. Morphology and lymph node pattern are the bedside discriminators within the painful ulcer group.

interactions.label: A 28-year-old woman in her second trimester is diagnosed with secondary syphilis

params.question: A 28-year-old woman in her second trimester is diagnosed with secondary syphilis and reports a confirmed penicillin allergy. What is the most appropriate management?

answers.text: Prescribe doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Doxycycline is teratogenic and contraindicated in pregnancy. It is the alternative for non-pregnant penicillin-allergic patients, but must never be used during pregnancy.

answers.text: Desensitise the patient to penicillin and treat with benzathine penicillin G

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In pregnancy, penicillin is the only acceptable treatment for syphilis. A penicillin-allergic pregnant patient must undergo desensitisation, never be switched to doxycycline, because untreated maternal syphilis causes congenital syphilis.

answers.text: Defer treatment until after delivery to avoid the risk of anaphylaxis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Deferring treatment allows the infection to progress and risks congenital syphilis in the foetus. The correct approach is to desensitise the patient and treat with penicillin during pregnancy itself.

answers.text: Prescribe erythromycin as a safer alternative during pregnancy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Erythromycin does not cross the placenta reliably and therefore does not adequately treat foetal infection. Penicillin after desensitisation remains the standard of care.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: in pregnancy, penicillin is the only acceptable treatment for syphilis. An allergic pregnant patient is desensitised, never switched to an alternative.
Exactly right. Penicillin is the only drug that treats both maternal and foetal syphilis; desensitisation is mandatory when allergy is present.

params.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between the inguinal swelling seen in lymphogranuloma venereum and that seen in donovanosis?

answers.text: LGV causes bilateral non-tender nodes, whereas donovanosis causes unilateral tender nodes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This description better fits the contrast between syphilis (bilateral non-tender) and chancroid (unilateral tender). The key LGV-versus-donovanosis distinction is the nature of the swelling itself — true node inflammation versus subcutaneous granulation.

answers.text: LGV causes true lymph node inflammation, whereas donovanosis produces a pseudobubo from subcutaneous granulation tissue

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In LGV, the inguinal lymph nodes themselves become inflamed and may suppurate. In donovanosis, the swelling is a pseudobubo — subcutaneous granulation tissue that mimics lymph node enlargement but does not arise from the nodes.

answers.text: LGV produces painless swelling, whereas donovanosis always presents with a draining sinus

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: LGV buboes are typically painful and may suppurate. A draining sinus is not a defining feature of donovanosis. The key distinction is true lymphadenitis versus pseudobubo.

answers.text: Both conditions produce identical inguinal swellings that can only be distinguished by serology

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The swellings differ in nature: LGV involves true lymph node inflammation, while donovanosis produces a pseudobubo from subcutaneous granulation tissue. This distinction can be appreciated clinically.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key point: LGV causes true lymph node inflammation (lymphadenitis), whereas donovanosis produces a pseudobubo — subcutaneous granulation tissue that mimics a lymph node swelling.
Correct — the true bubo versus pseudobubo distinction is the hallmark difference between these two conditions.

interactions.label: Bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis, and cervicitis are the three common causes

params.question: Bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis, and cervicitis are the three common causes of pathological vaginal discharge. Which of the following correctly links a condition to its most significant consequence?

answers.text: Bacterial vaginosis increases the risk of preterm labour and HIV susceptibility

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Bacterial vaginosis disrupts the normal vaginal flora, which raises the risk of preterm labour in pregnant women and increases susceptibility to HIV infection. This is why it requires treatment even when symptoms seem mild.

answers.text: Trichomoniasis commonly progresses to pelvic inflammatory disease

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: It is cervicitis — not trichomoniasis — that can silently ascend to cause pelvic inflammatory disease. Trichomoniasis increases the likelihood of HIV transmission, which is its key public health consequence.

answers.text: Cervicitis is the leading cause of preterm delivery in Indian women

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Preterm delivery risk is primarily associated with bacterial vaginosis, not cervicitis. The danger of cervicitis lies in its silent progression to pelvic inflammatory disease, which can threaten future fertility.

answers.text: Bacterial vaginosis reduces the efficacy of antiretroviral therapy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Bacterial vaginosis increases susceptibility to acquiring HIV, but it does not reduce antiretroviral efficacy. Its key consequences are preterm labour risk and increased HIV susceptibility.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the specific consequences: bacterial vaginosis → preterm labour and HIV susceptibility; trichomoniasis → HIV transmission; cervicitis → pelvic inflammatory disease.
Well done. Each condition has distinct consequences: BV raises preterm and HIV risk, trichomoniasis facilitates HIV transmission, and cervicitis can progress to PID.

interactions.label: After prescribing syndromic treatment for urethral discharge, which set of addit

params.question: After prescribing syndromic treatment for urethral discharge, which set of additional steps completes the 4 Cs framework recommended by NACO?

answers.text: Culture confirmation, compliance counselling, condom demonstration, and case notification

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Culture confirmation is not one of the 4 Cs. The syndromic approach specifically works without waiting for culture results. The first C stands for contact tracing, not culture.

answers.text: Contact tracing, counselling, compliance, and condoms

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The 4 Cs are: Contact tracing (issuing contact slips to partners), Counselling (about the disease and safe behaviour), Compliance (ensuring the full course of treatment is completed), and Condoms (promoting consistent use). Every STI visit should also include an offer of HIV testing.

answers.text: Clinical staging, contact tracing, co-trimoxazole prophylaxis, and condoms

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Clinical staging and co-trimoxazole prophylaxis belong to HIV management, not to the STI syndromic management framework. The 4 Cs are contact tracing, counselling, compliance, and condoms.

answers.text: Contact tracing, confirmatory serology, condoms, and compulsory partner treatment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Confirmatory serology is not part of the 4 Cs, and partner treatment is offered through contact slips, not compulsory measures. The second C is counselling and the third is compliance with the prescribed regimen.

overallFeedback.feedback: The 4 Cs are: Contact tracing, Counselling, Compliance, and Condoms. Together with HIV testing, they complete the syndromic management approach at every STI consultation.
Exactly right. The 4 Cs ensure that treatment extends beyond the index patient to break the chain of transmission.
